chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Hamza ibn Abdillah al-Ja'fari, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Hamza, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who recognizes Allah fears Allah, and the one who fears Allah, his soul becomes indifferent to the world.'
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between knowing God and detaching from the world in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) outlines a spiritual causal chain where true recognition of God (ma'rifah) leads to fear of Him, which in turn leads to detachment from the worldly life. This teaching emphasizes that intellectual and spiritual awareness of the Divine naturally cultivates piety and asceticism, a concept central to Shia gnosis (irfan) where knowledge is not merely theoretical but transformative. The hadith highlights that fear (khawf) acts as the bridge between knowing God and renouncing worldly attachments, a key theme in the chapter on fear and hope.
